q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of Indian sweets?
title: Indian sweets carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the main ingredients per kg of sweets, such as milk or khoa, sugar, ghee, flour and nuts, using supplier figures. Add the kitchen's fuel and electricity per kg made, then the boxes.

ul: Milk, khoa or paneer for milk sweets.
Sugar, ghee or oil, flour, gram flour and nuts.
Cooking and frying on LPG or PNG.

p: Report per kg by sweet type, since milk and ghee based sweets usually carry more footprint than flour and sugar based ones.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 7,310 / 6,000 = 1.218 kg CO2 per kg
Add milk, ghee, sugar and nuts for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
